text:
c.jones: hey team — we're getting intermittent 400s from the embeddings endpoint since we bumped max_batch_size -> 128 and enabled dynamic batching. Error: \"dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 1024\". Started ~1h ago, ~5% of calls failing, tail latency spikes too. Example request id: req_2004578_42. Can someone help triage?

alice.chen: thanks for flagging — can you paste a minimal repro (curl) and one of the failing request_ids + approximate timestamps? also which model name/version are you calling?

c.jones: sending curl (redacted keys):

```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rw-embed-1","input":["hello world","short text"],"max_batch_size":128,"dynamic_batching":true}'
```

Failing req ids: req_2004578_42 (2026-03-17T10:18:24Z), req_2004578_89 (2026-03-17T10:22:11Z). Total volume small — ~200 rps to embeddings service.

infra-bot: model-deploy-notice: rw-embed-1 variant rollout started at 2026-03-17T09:55:00Z; target traffic split: v1=40% (dim=1536), v2=60% (dim=1024).

priya_sre: looking at runtime logs now — I can reproduce a failing batch. The dynamic batcher is coalescing requests across variants when max_batch_size is high and variant-selection is per-request. We have logs showing a single batch with mixed variant entries:

```
[10:18:24.123] batch_id=blk_789 entries=64 variants=[v1,v2,v1,...]
[10:18:24.124] concat_inputs -> attempted concat -> error: embed_dim_mismatch expected=1536 actual=1024
```

priya_sre: appears the batcher concatenates inputs before checking variant compatibility. That explains both the dimension mismatch and the tail latency spike (failed batches require fallback and retry).

marco: +1. immediate mitigation: set per-model-variant batching or prevent cross-variant coalescing. For customers: recommend pinning to a single variant or temporarily set `dynamic_batching=false` or reduce `max_batch_size` to avoid mixing.

alice.chen: escalated to eng-runtime (SUP-12345). Marco — can you confirm whether we should rollback v2 or patch the batcher? Which is faster?

marco: rollback of v2 -> v1 routing to 100% is fastest short-term (few mins to change traffic split). Patch to batcher to check dims before concat will take a couple of hours + QA. I'll prepare a hotfix branch that rejects mixed-variant batches and triggers single-request fallback rather than concatenation.

c.jones: can you recommend the least-disruptive customer-side change? We have many clients using the default model name.

priya_sre: customer-side workaround: set `model` to the explicit variant (e.g., `rw-embed-1@v1`) or set `dynamic_batching:false` and `max_batch_size:32`. That should eliminate the mixed-variant path.

c.jones: trying `dynamic_batching:false` + `max_batch_size:32` now. will report back. thanks. :pray:

alice.chen: for our logs / postmortem, please also attach the failing request bodies if you can. If you can't include payloads, at least give the request_ids and we can pull server-side payloads.

c.jones: attached req bodies for the two failing ids in the ticket. After switching to dynamic_batching=false + max_batch_size=32 the errors dropped to 0 in the last 15m — confirming workaround works.

priya_sre: noted. runtime team will: (1) rollback v2 to v1 for rw-embed-1 to stop customer impact, (2) push hotfix to batcher to validate dims before concat and treat mixed batches as non-coalescible, (3) add a server-side metric for `mixed_variant_batch_rejects`.

marco: quick repro for eng QA if you need to reproduce locally: run two model variants locally with different embed dims and run a client that sets `model` field per-request but allows dynamic batching. Use a high max_batch_size and emit many concurrent requests. Example harness: 

```
# pseudo-harness
python3 harness.py --variants v1=1536,v2=1024 --clients 100 --max_batch_size 128 --dynamic true
```

marco: saving logs & patch draft in SUP-12345. Will monitor rollback impact.

alice.chen: closing loop with customer in the ticket. thanks everyone for quick triage. :thumbsup:

c.jones: huge thanks — the workaround is fine for now. Please keep me posted when rollback/patch is live.
